Team / Tim — I reviewed the spreadsheet and drafted a focused redline (MSA_Security_Redlines_v1.docx) that:

- Maps each Acme question to the exhibit clause (see column mapping in the doc).
- Recommends language for SOC 2 scope: Redwood will provide SOC 2 Type II report upon request for customers with an executed DPA and NDA in place; the report is shared under a restricted access process, not broadly published.
- Proposes pen-test wording:
  • Redwood permits customer-contracted third-party penetration tests limited to non-production staging environments.
  • Tests must be scheduled within a defined 48–72h notice window, and Redwood requires a point-of-contact for coordination.
  • Testers will be provided ephemeral credentials and will not be allowed lateral movement beyond defined staging subnets; any change to scope requires 7 days' written notice.
- Evidence cadence options: quarterly snapshot (default) or on-demand with 10 business day turnaround (paid add-on for expedited requests).

For operations, we recommend two staging access windows per quarter and a short runbook for evidence delivery (we'll attach a proposed runbook to the DocuSign/HubSpot record).

Next asks for Acme: please confirm that staging scoping above is acceptable and provide your preferred evidence cadence ("quarterly" or "on-demand"). Once we have that, Laura and I will finalize the redline and flag any legal trade-offs (SLA, liability carveouts).

Connor O'Brien
Senior Counsel (Commercial Contracts) — Redwood Inference
